files.name: Voice test E — Bark with [laughs] cue
files.note: Cat line rewritten as 'Hey, Mouse! [laughs] I'm going to catch you!'. Bark inserted two hesitation sounds ('Um', 'Uh') and dropped the word 'you', so the cue is NOT clean on bark-small. Listen at ~1-2s and judge whether the 'Uh' is a usable chuckle. Cat preset here is speaker_6, not speaker_3 as in test D.

files.name: Voice test D — BARK (expressive engine)
files.note: Same three lines on Bark instead of Kokoro. Cat 113 Hz median, mouse 248 Hz — 135 Hz apart. Pitch range 308/369 Hz vs 148/152 on Kokoro, so roughly double the melodic movement. Loudness matched to C2 (-22.2 LUFS) for a fair A/B. Costs ~2-3 min per line on CPU.

files.name: Voice test C2 — ACTED (Fenrir / Jessica)
files.note: Same two voices as test C, but directed: per-beat rate, pitch lift with formant preservation, stressed words +2-4 dB, two real inhales, exact pauses. Cat pitch range +41%, mouse +29% brighter.

files.name: Voice test C — Fenrir / Jessica
files.note: Cat am_fenrir 133 Hz, mouse af_jessica 205 Hz — two high-energy voices, Jessica is the fastest talker in the pool. Fenrir is hot and needed peak-capping.

files.name: Voice test B — George / Isabella
files.note: Cat bm_george 145 Hz — warm British storyteller. Mouse bf_isabella 202 Hz. Softest and most nursery-friendly; narrower 57 Hz gap.

files.name: Voice test A — Puck / Bella
files.note: Cat am_puck 110 Hz — bright, energetic, cheekiest of the three. Mouse af_bella 197 Hz. Widest pitch gap at 87 Hz, easiest for a 3-6 year old to follow who is talking.

files.name: The Cat and the Clever Mouse — Episode 1
files.note: First full episode. Narrated by af_heart (approved), so no lip sync needed. 5 shots, 4 hard cuts, iris out. Original rigs, background, MIDI score and SFX all generated locally. Free/offline throughout.

files.name: Pip and the Snail — v4 (HyperFrames + Rhubarb)
files.note: Five shots, three hard cuts, close-up on the face. Articulated 8-part fox rig with knee joints, lids, brows and a hinged jaw driven by Rhubarb. Snail voiced separately.

files.name: Narration C — Onyx (low male)
files.note: Same narration, lower and slower. Most 'storybook at bedtime' of the three.

files.name: Narration B — Heart (warm female)
files.note: Same narration, warmer female storyteller. Fastest read of the three.

files.name: Narration A — George (warm British male)
files.note: Storyteller version. 'A cat chased a little mouse along the sunny footpath. The mouse was quick. The cat was sure he would catch him. But the mouse was faster than he looked.'
